title: Mechanism
description: A candidate or ground-truth reaction network. State variables are concentrations in mM of nitrogen-equivalents (mM-N). All stoichiometry is written per N-equivalent, so N is conserved when the coefficients on both sides sum to the same number. H, O and charge balance are implicit (water, H+/OH-, electrons) and are not tracked; electron count is tracked via nitrogen oxidation states.

motif.description: Coarse branching motif, used for reporting benchmark results by motif.

conservation.description: Element balance instead of N-equivalents (non-electrochemical domains). Amounts are formula units on the dataset basis, every species declares its composition, and every reaction conserves sum(coeff * composition[e]) for each listed element.

sinks_to_unobserved.description: Optional: species ids that are real products but not measured in the lab setup (e.g. N2, N2O in an aqueous-only analysis).

observable.description: False means the species exists in the model but is never measured.

n_N_per_molecule.description: N atoms per molecule, used only to convert reported units to mM-N (e.g. N2 -> 2).

N_oxidation_state.description: Mean oxidation state of N. NO3- +5, NO2- +3, NO +2, N2O +1, N2 0, NH2OH -1, NH3/NH4+ -3. Null if unknown (hidden intermediates).

composition.description: Atoms per formula unit of the conserved elements (mechanism.conservation), e.g. {"Ti": 5, "Li": 4} for Li4Ti5O12. Non-integer values express non-stoichiometry, e.g. Li-deficient Li2-xTiO3.

electrons.description: Electrons consumed per reaction event (N-equivalent basis). Null if not applicable or unknown. Checked against oxidation states when all are known.

source.description: Where the value came from, e.g. 'Katsounaros 2012 Table 1'.

tie.description: Optional tie group. Parameters with the same tie name in one mechanism are one free parameter (same kind, bounds and fixed status), e.g. a catalyst-state time constant shared by several steps. Counts once in model comparison.

family.description: mass_action: r = k * prod(c_i ^ coeff_i) over reactants. power_law: r = k * prod(c_i ^ order_i) with orders given or free. langmuir_saturation: r = k * c / (1 + c / K) for the single reactant.

orders.description: Reaction orders per reactant species (power_law only). Default for mass_action is the stoichiometric coefficient.

k_mt.description: Optional mass-transport rate constant. Effective k = 1/(1/k + 1/k_mt).

potential_dependence.description: k(E) = k * exp(alpha * F * (E_ref - E) / (R * T)). E in V vs RHE. alpha is a lumped effective transfer coefficient (slope of ln k vs -E times RT/F), so it need not lie in (0,1).

E_ref_V.description: Potential (V vs RHE) at which k is quoted.

time_modulation.description: Catalyst-state factor g(t) multiplying k. activation: g = 1 - exp(-t/tau) (induction period). deactivation: g = exp(-t/tau) (fouling, pH drift, surface reconstruction). Added after real-data calibration: Liao 2025 Supp. Fig. 49 needs activation (tau about 70 min) and Supp. Fig. 50 needs deactivation (tau about 300-500 min). Also the hook for a catalyst-phase vector that evolves in time. avrami: nucleation-and-growth (JMAK) form using the step's own k and an Avrami exponent n, g = n * (k t)^(n-1), so a lone first-order step A -> B follows alpha = 1 - exp(-(k t)^n) from t = 0, the common time origin (e.g. insertion into the hot zone). n = 1 is plain first order, n < 1 decelerating (diffusion-limited), n > 1 sigmoidal.

temperature_dependence.description: Arrhenius: k(T) = k * exp(-Ea/R * (1/T - 1/T_ref)), so k is quoted at T_ref. A free Ea needs data at two or more temperatures.
